title: Cyber Resilience Act - Conformity assessment (Shaping Europe's digital future)
key_claim: Under the CRA, critical products (such as smart cards, secure elements and smart meter gateways) must always undergo mandatory third-party conformity assessment by a notified body, and important products need one where harmonised standards are not applied; the Commission's NANDO register will list CRA notified bodies only once they are available.
frame_summary: The Commission argues the CRA legally requires third-party notified-body conformity assessment for whole product classes, even though those bodies do not yet exist.
verbatim_quote: Critical products (e.g., smart cards, secure elements, smart meter gateways): The use of a notified body is mandatory in any case.
notes: Tier-1 legal basis: mandatory notified-body assessment for CRA critical products. Quote fetched and read verbatim on the live page during sourcing (2026-07-20); sandbox egress returns 403 so the provenance audit reports UNVERIFIED, not FAIL.

title: Cyber Resilience Act - Implementation timeline (Shaping Europe's digital future)
key_claim: The Commission's official CRA timeline shows the notified-body/CAB notification rules only starting to apply on 11 June 2026, Member States targeted to notify sufficient conformity assessment bodies by 11 December 2026, first standardisation deliverables in Q3 2026 with more by 30 October 2027, and full application of the CRA on 11 December 2027.
frame_summary: The Commission's own timeline shows the certification machinery (bodies plus standards) only switching on in mid-2026 and not maturing until 2027.
verbatim_quote: Notification of sufficient Conformity Assessment Bodies across Member States

title: Technical Competence Requirements for CRA Notified Bodies
key_claim: In June 2026 ENISA published the baseline technical competence requirements that conformity assessment bodies must meet to become CRA notified bodies, noting these must be complemented by competences to demonstrate conformity with harmonised standards that are currently under development.
frame_summary: ENISA argues even the criteria for who can become a CRA notified body are only being set now, and depend on standards that do not yet exist.
verbatim_quote: These competences need to be complemented with the specific competences required to demonstrate conformity of products with the harmonised standards that are currently under development.

title: Artificial intelligence: Council and Parliament agree to simplify and streamline rules
date_evidence: Dateline 'Council of the EU - Press release - 7 May 2026'; meta SORT_DATE 20260507
key_claim: Co-legislators reached a provisional agreement on the Digital Omnibus deferring the AI Act's high-risk obligations to fixed new dates of 2 December 2027 (stand-alone, Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (embedded in products, Annex I), with the rules to start applying once the Commission confirms the needed standards and tools are available.
frame_summary: The Council frames the deferral as simplification and explicitly ties the timing of high-risk rules to the availability of standards and tools.
verbatim_quote: the new application dates would be 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in products.

title: European standardization in flux: Navigating delegation and control in AI governance
key_claim: The EU delegates detailed, politically charged AI rule-making to private standards bodies; the Commission's tactics to retain control over that delegated rule-making risk the integrity and legitimacy of European standardisation.
frame_summary: The authors argue that outsourcing operative AI rule-making to private standardisation is a legitimacy problem, not a neutral technical step.
verbatim_quote: the EU has a range of robust tactics to interfere in technical standard-setting, but in opting to deploy these tactics, might risk the overall integrity and legitimacy of European standardization more broadly.

title: EU AI Act Update: Timeline Relief, Targeted Simplification, and New Prohibitions
key_claim: Covington sets out the 'timeline relief plus targeted simplification' package: Annex III high-risk obligations postponed from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027 (16 months) and Annex I from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028, with the delay giving standards-setting bodies such as CEN-CENELEC additional time to prepare the standards that serve as the backbone of the requirements.

title: EU AI Act Conformity Assessment: What to Do When the Infrastructure Isn't Ready
key_claim: As of April 2026 zero notified bodies are formally designated in NANDO for AI Act conformity assessments, no harmonised standards have been published in the Official Journal, and no Article 41 common specifications exist, so the AI Act's conformity-assessment infrastructure does not yet exist.
frame_summary: Reg Intel argues the AI Act's certification capacity is effectively zero, leaving systems that need third-party assessment without a route to certification.
verbatim_quote: As of April 2026, zero notified bodies are formally designated in NANDO for AI Act conformity assessments.

title: EU MDR Notified Body Capacity Crisis 2026-2027: Manufacturer Action Plan
key_claim: The European Commission's 18th Notified Bodies Survey (March 2026, data through October 2025) shows 33,175 MDR applications against only 17,549 certificates issued and 3,634 IVDR applications against 2,194 certificates, leaving an estimated 15,000-plus applications pending across 51 active notified bodies, with reviews taking 13 to 18 months.
frame_summary: MedDeviceGuide documents the MDR/IVDR notified-body backlog as a concrete precedent for a mandatory third-party assessment regime producing a multi-year certification bottleneck and market-access risk.
verbatim_quote: On the medical device side, 33,175 applications have been submitted to Notified Bodies, but only 17,549 MDR certificates have been issued.
notes: Tier-3 historical parallel with hard numbers; the MDR/IVDR backlog is the template the AI Act and CRA risk repeating. Quote fetched and read verbatim on the live page during sourcing (2026-07-20); sandbox egress returns 403 so the provenance audit reports UNVERIFIED, not FAIL.
